# Run comparison view with multi-select in the Dashboard

## Description

This epic delivers the core experiment-comparison capability in the Dashboard:
users can select two or more training and pipeline runs from the runs list and
view their parameters and metrics side by side. Today, parameters and
metrics live only on per-run pages, forcing comparison into exported
spreadsheets; this epic brings that comparison in-platform.

## Scope

- Multi-select of two or more runs (training and pipeline runs) from the
  Dashboard runs list.
- A comparison view that renders the selected runs' parameters and metrics
  side by side.
- Retrieval of the selected runs' parameters and metrics from the existing
  run data surfaced by Data Science Pipelines (passive component — no DSP
  code changes are in scope; see acceptance criteria).

Out of scope (per strategy): automatic best-run selection or promotion, and
comparison across clusters or across projects.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given the Dashboard runs list, when the user selects two or more runs, then
  a comparison view opens showing each selected run's parameters and metrics
  side by side.
- Given runs whose parameters and metrics are stored via Data Science
  Pipelines, when they are selected for comparison, then their parameters and
  metrics render correctly using the existing DSP run data interfaces
  (validation that DSP keeps working unmodified as the data source).
- The comparison view is reachable from the runs list for both training and
  pipeline runs.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-1 (P0): select two or more runs and view parameters and metrics side by
  side in the Dashboard — fully covered by this epic.
- HLR-3 (P1): the run diff view is a separately planned follow-on epic that
  extends this comparison view; it is not part of this epic's scope.

# Record originating run linkage on registered model versions

## Description

This epic delivers run lineage in the Model Registry: a registered model
version records a link back to the run that produced it, so that downstream
consumers (such as the Dashboard's registry UI) can resolve the originating
run and open a comparison of candidate runs. Model promotion decisions need
this connection between registered versions and the experiments that produced
them.

## Scope

- Record, on a registered model version, a reference to the run that produced
  it, using the Model Registry's existing model-version metadata extension
  point (custom properties) or an equivalent registry-native mechanism — the
  concrete representation is an implementation decision for the Model Registry
  team.
- Make the recorded run linkage retrievable through the Model Registry REST
  API so clients can resolve the originating run for any registered model
  version.
- Registration flows (or registrating users/tools) are able to supply the
  originating run reference when a version is registered.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a model version produced by a run, when the version is registered,
  then the registered version carries a link back to that run.
- Given a registered model version with a recorded run link, when a client
  queries the Model Registry REST API, then the run linkage is returned and
  the originating run can be resolved.
- The linkage mechanism is documented in the Model Registry API surface (e.g.
  OpenAPI spec) so consumers can build against it.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-2 (P1, data side): registered model versions link back to the run that
  produced them — the linkage recording and API retrieval half of this HLR is
  covered by this epic; the registry-UI entry point that consumes it is
  covered by the Dashboard-side work.

# Open a run comparison from the Model Registry UI

## Description

This epic delivers the Model Registry side of the comparison workflow in the
Dashboard: from a registered model version in the registry UI, a user can open
the run comparison view for the run that produced that version. This lets data
scientists start a comparison while reviewing registered models, without going
back to the runs list, using the run lineage recorded on model versions by the
Model Registry.

## Scope

- In the Dashboard's Model Registry UI, surface the originating run of a
  registered model version using the run linkage exposed by the Model Registry
  REST API.
- Add an action on a registered model version (and/or its registered model)
  that opens the run comparison view with the linked run preselected, so a
  comparison can be started directly from the registry.
- Preselecting a run from the registry composes with the comparison view's
  existing multi-select behavior (the user adds further runs to compare
  against).

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a registered model version that records a link to its originating
  run, when the user views that version in the Model Registry UI, then the
  originating run is visible/resolvable from the version.
- Given a registered model version with a recorded run link, when the user
  chooses to open a comparison from the registry, then the comparison view
  opens with the linked run preselected and ready to compare against other
  runs.
- Given a registered model version with no recorded run link, when the user
  views it in the registry UI, then the comparison entry point degrades
  gracefully (unavailable or clearly disabled) rather than erroring.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-2 (P1, UI side): "a comparison can be opened from the Model Registry" —
  the registry entry point half of this HLR is covered by this epic; it
  depends on the run-linkage data recorded by the Model Registry work and on
  the comparison view delivered by the Dashboard comparison work.

# Run diff view between two selected runs

## Description

This epic delivers the run diff view: for two selected runs, the Dashboard
highlights which parameters and metrics changed between them, so data
scientists can see at a glance what differs between candidate runs when making
model promotion decisions. The diff view builds on the run comparison view
delivered by the Dashboard comparison work — it extends that existing surface
with a diff mode rather than building a second comparison surface.

## Scope

- A diff mode within the run comparison view that, for two selected runs,
  highlights which parameters and metrics changed between them.
- Changed and unchanged parameters and metrics are distinguishable from one
  another in the diff display.
- The diff mode operates on the same run parameter/metric data already
  rendered by the comparison view (no separate data retrieval path).

Out of scope (per strategy): automatic best-run selection or promotion, and
comparison across clusters or across projects.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given the run comparison view with two runs selected, when the user switches
  to the diff view, then the parameters and metrics that differ between the
  two runs are highlighted, and unchanged ones are distinguishable from
  changed ones.
- Given the run comparison view with two runs whose parameters and metrics are
  stored via Data Science Pipelines, when the user opens the diff view, then
  the diff renders correctly using the run data already surfaced by the
  comparison view.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-3 (P1): run diff view highlighting changed parameters and metrics
  between two selected runs — fully covered by this epic. This epic extends
  the run comparison view delivered by the Dashboard comparison work and
  depends on it.

# Decomposition Summary — RHAISTRAT-9015: Experiment comparison for training and pipeline runs

Triage: full decomposition (not below-threshold, not docs-only). The strategy
spans multiple components and teams (Dashboard, Model Registry, Data Science
Pipelines), and HLR-4 calls for substantive documentation authoring — a
distinct work stream — so the below-threshold escape conditions do not apply.

## Step 1 — Strategy structure

The strategy is minimal. Present: Problem Statement, High-Level Requirements
(HLR-1..HLR-4 with priorities), Affected Components (bare list), Out of Scope,
Open Questions (none). Missing sections (health warnings, decomposition

- Affected Components has no per-component change description or owner team.

All three components exist in `.context/architecture-context/` (rhoai-3.0) and

**Passive component note (Data Science Pipelines):** the strategy lists DSP as
